messages.text: Ok, I like the plan, go loose

I’ll synchronize with the merged envelope baseline, start a research branch, and launch the first increment: six candidate definitions, a verified ACTS environment, and benchmarked solenoid fields and propagation. The team will develop the subsystem assessments alongside the software work.

The research branch now includes the merged envelope baseline and the new dashboard work. The architect, physics, and software agents are working on candidate definitions, comparison criteria, and ACTS setup. I’m building the independent solenoid benchmark to check the field calculation before we use it for propagation studies.
Can you do `pip install pyacts` instead ?
I’ll check `pyacts` and try installing it in an isolated environment. If it provides the tracking ACTS bindings, we’ll use it for the propagation tests.

You’re right: the [official ACTS repository](https://github.com/acts-project/acts) recommends `pip install pyacts`, imported as `acts`. I’ve corrected the plan, and the software agent is installing it. The independent inner- and outer-solenoid calculations have passed their first numerical checks.

The first field result shows why we need spatial maps: the inner-solenoid vacuum model falls from 3 T at the centre to about 1.77 T on axis at the tracker’s forward edge. The larger outer-coil control gives about 2.74 T there, but needs more space and current. The team also flagged that its proposed coil would occupy one of the common muon diagnostic surfaces; that surface cannot count as a physical measurement in this configuration.

`pyacts==47.7.0` is installed in `reference/cache/acts-venv`. Importing `acts` works, and the solenoid field, straight-line stepper, and Runge–Kutta stepper are available. I’m continuing with numerical propagation checks before calling the setup verified.

All subsystem assessments are now documented. Independent physics review confirmed the sampled field values with a finer calculation. The field plots explicitly mask regions that have not converged near the idealized coils. I’m collecting the candidate cards, plots, ACTS checks, and open questions into the first research PR.

The remaining check is the ACTS propagation API: it must reproduce known straight lines and helices, including the charge and field signs. The source catalogue, session log, and dashboard now include DES-004; the envelope baseline remains unchanged.

ACTS has now reproduced the straight-line and uniform-field helix fixtures, including reversed charge and field. The setup record will include the exact package version, commands, and numerical limits. I’m doing the final integration checks and preparing the draft PR for review of this first increment.

The first increment is ready: six candidate cards, five specialist assessments, two field plots, and a working `pyacts` environment. All six field tests, seven ACTS propagation fixtures, and five ACTS solenoid-axis checks passed, along with the repository checks. I’m committing and opening the draft PR; it makes no architecture selection or sign-off claim.

[Draft PR #6](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/6) is open, and its initial CI build passed. I’m finishing the dashboard’s pending-review record and final log update. The next discussion is about the candidate definitions and comparison contract, especially the outer coil’s space requirements.

Installed **`pyacts==47.7.0`** successfully; `import acts` works.

The first research increment is in **[draft PR #6](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/6)**:

- Six magnetic candidates and subsystem assessments.
- Solenoid field plots and reproducible benchmarks.
- Seven ACTS propagation checks and five solenoid-axis comparisons—all passed.
- Updated sources, session logs and dashboard.

CI passed; working tree is clean on `research/magnetic-configurations`.

Next review: the comparison contract and outer-coil space amendment, before iron/yoke and toroid studies.
